about: The shared rule set for what a neutral build (the app without our brand layer) must not carry and must carry. Layers B (the family's identity) and C (the publisher's service) are maintained by Brand; every change is read by Brand. Prose and reasons: docs/neutral-build-brand-and-scan-20261118.md. Shaped like PLC's plc-neutrality/1 (id, pattern, flags, why) so the shared engine can load it; each application adds its own productNames, ownDomains, allowed and allowedHosts in its own config. Severity 'fail' fails the scan from day one; 'warn' is reported and reviewed by a person. scope 'all' = every text file; scope 'visible' = text a person reads (HTML text nodes, titles, alt text, markdown, txt, UI string tables), where the engine can tell, else 'all'.

layers.B: the family's identity (never in a neutral build)
layers.C: the publisher's service (never in a neutral build)

strings.why: The parent's name in any spelling (spaced, hyphenated, joined). Allowed only in attributionPaths, in the one fixed attribution block. The existing PLC rule matched only the joined form.
The programme's internal name appears in no public build. No allow-list.

Another family project's name is family navigation. The application's own name comes from its productNames setting and is exempt; any other use is an allow-list entry by path with a reason (userVisible:true needs a reason Brand reads).

Every host we run. Allowed only: the source URL of the attribution block; a disclosed, changeable default listed with a reason and, if temporary, an until. Lower case only: hosts are lower case, and the product name PrivateLocal.Chat is not a host.

The maintainer's names. Real people's names only in licence-required notices (allow-list by path with a reason). The project's own repository path is allowed by path. (mailto links are the separate rule mailto-link.)

An actual mailto link (an HTML href or a markdown link): a support or contact address is the publisher's. The string 'mailto:' inside code that decides how to render someone else's link is not a link of ours and does not match.
An e-mail address: a support address is layer C. Licence and copyright texts carry author addresses legitimately: allow by path with a reason.
Internal machines, tools, agent files and commit trailers. A download never carries development tooling.
Planning-board ids in prose. Warn: short codes occur in code and data legitimately.
A planning-board reference in shipped text or code comments (found in PLC's neutral build: 'board T444'). Internal process, never public.
Analytics, tracking and third-party error reporting. A neutral build collects nothing and contacts none.
Fonts and scripts fetched at run time from a third party. A neutral build loads nothing it does not ship (a licence text naming such a host is an allow-list entry).
Support, community and social links are the publisher's. A neutral build points to the source repository and nothing else.
The packet's namespaced tokens and font family names: the family's visual identity.
The family palette. May coincide innocently; a person reviews. A neutral build uses plain colours.
The family's display face. A neutral build uses system fonts; an app that needs a face says why in its allow-list.
Claims of a relationship or standing we do not have for someone else's copy.

Promises and absolutes about privacy, security or hosting; and 'sovereign' about a product (it is only said about people, in our own statements of purpose). Visible text only: licence texts that 'guarantee your freedom' are not ours (allow by path).
Hype. The voice is plain and concrete.

strings.pattern: \bcontact us\b|\bjoin us\b|\bsubscribe to\b|\bnewsletter\b|\bfollow us\b|\bsign up\b|\bcoming soon\b|\broadmap\b
strings.why: Marketing, community and plans: the publisher's voice, or a feature that is not in this build.
Unqualified evidence words (packet rule: nothing is called these without its own evidence). The licence phrase 'free software' and technical uses are allowed by path with a reason.
No setting, option or manifest field may rename the app or hide the attribution block.

binaryAssets.why: Brand marks, icons and fonts are matched by SHA-256 against the packet manifests, so renamed copies are caught, including binaries a text scan cannot read. Every file path and hash in these manifests is a brand asset; a match fails the scan unless the application's allow-list names it with a reason.

checks.why: A title line: the app name and version.
The attribution phrase, plain text, lower case, no logo, no link.
The source: the forge repository or the per-build archive the build metadata names (the URL names the build id or the commit).

mustContain.why: One record that the scan and the About page read.
If the target has an About or Help page it carries the block.

rules.noAddressWithoutManifest: For the app and runkit targets no canonical, Open Graph, structured data, sitemap, robots or feed may carry an address (PLC's rule, kept).

exceptionShape.userVisible: true when the path is text a person reads; needs a reason Brand reads
exceptionShape.until: task id or date for a temporary exception

visibleScopeNote: scope 'visible' means: text a person reads. For HTML, the text nodes, title, alt and aria-label text with scripts and styles removed; for .md and .txt the whole file; never LICENSE*, THIRD-PARTY*, NOTICE licence sections or vendor/ trees (those are allow-listed by path).

attributionExemption.why: The attribution block necessarily names us and our forge. The exemption is narrow so it cannot hide anything else.
onlyFor: the line 'from ai of our own'
the Source: URL (or the link in the About region) matching the source-line pattern in mustContain
attributionExemption.notFor: any other text in those files: a second mention of our name or a second host in NOTICE.md, README.md, about or help is still a failure; the app's own product name is exempt through productNames, not through this.

stability.format: neutrality-rules/1 is frozen: field names in this file will not be renamed or removed. Changes are additive (new optional fields, new rules). A breaking change bumps the format to neutrality-rules/2 with a migration note and Brand tells the engine's owner first. The rules' contents (which patterns exist) change with `version`; the engine prints the version it ran.
stability.readBy: the shared scan engine (PLC extraction into /cosmoshot/delivery-tooling, T736/T740); devops vendors the file; Brand maintains layers B and C and reads every diff

html.textNodes: every text node outside script, style and template; noscript content counts
attributes: value (on input type=submit|button|reset and on button)
content (on meta name=description, meta property=og:title|og:description|og:image:alt, meta name=twitter:title|twitter:description)
html.jsonLd: string values of name, headline, description and alternateName in application/ld+json blocks (a neutral build should have none that carries an address)

visibleScope.json: manifest.webmanifest and similar web manifests: the string values of name, short_name and description
visibleScope.appProvided: an application lists further UI string tables in its own exceptions file under `visibleFiles` (globs); JS and JSON files are not visible by default (too noisy), and text only in code comments is covered by the scope-all rules, not the voice lint

attributionRegions.why: In about, help and README the family-name and our-hosts exemption applies only inside the attribution region, so a second mention elsewhere still fails.
attributionRegions.markdownAndText: the lines from 'from ai of our own' through the 'Source:' line, contiguous
attributionRegions.mustEqualRecord: the region's name, version, commit, licence and source must equal attribution.json (the engine checks this itself)

engineCalls.attribution: The engine CALLS `python3 /cosmoshot/delivery-tooling/attribution/attribution.py check DIR_OR_ARCHIVE` (or the vendored copy) and uses its exit code and message for NOTICE.md, SOURCE.txt and attribution.json. One implementation of the narrow exemption; the engine does not reimplement it in Node. The engine itself handles only the HTML and markdown regions above (about, help, README) and must treat a missing attribution.py as a failure, never as a pass.

exceptionsFile.name: neutrality-exceptions.json in each application's repository

productNames: regexes for the application's own product names; removed from the text before the other-app-names rule runs
visibleFiles: optional globs of UI string tables to treat as visible

exceptions.rule: a rule id from the shared file
paths: globs relative to the build root
exceptions.userVisible: true if the matched text is read by a person; needs a reason Brand reads; default false

until.by: YYYY-MM-DD (an upper bound, at most 90 days ahead)

exceptions.match: optional regex tested against the TOKEN that contains each individual match (the maximal run of characters around it that are not whitespace, quotes, angle brackets or parentheses; for a URL, the whole URL). Every match is judged on its own token, never on its line: a second mention in the same line, or anywhere in a minified one-line file, is a separate match and still fails unless its own token satisfies the regex. Example: 'cdn\\.aiofourown\\.com/models/' covers the token 'https://cdn.aiofourown.com/models/' and not another URL on the same line.

rules: a path-scoped exception without a why fails
an exception that matches nothing fails the scan
an exception with until.by in the past FAILS the scan
an exception with until needs both task and by; a bare task id or a bare date is invalid
every exception with until is reported at every run, whether or not it matches (an 'until' list at the end of the output)

name-only brand asset matches (the binaryAssets.pathNames check) are warnings; an application's own mark that shares a generic file name (favicon.svg, wordmark-light.svg) and whose hash differs from every packet asset is listed as an exception with that why (layer A); a hash match is always a failure unless the application names the file

a default that points at our infrastructure and is disclosed on one page and changeable by one setting is a PERMANENT exception with no 'until'; 'until' is only for a default that cannot yet be changed
exception matching is per match, not per line (see `match`): this keeps an exception from masking other mentions in a minified or single-line file
